I'll start by reading the spec and tasks files.

1	---
2	feature: User question
3	status: approved
4	---
5	
6	# User question
7	
8	## Goal
9	A session that cannot proceed without a decision from the person running it asks a structured question instead of guessing or stopping with prose. The model issues a question request through a tool; the transcript shows it as a card with the question, its choices and a free-text alternative; the person answers and the answer returns to the model as the tool's own result, so the session continues in the same turn. This exists so that plan sessions (which are blind and therefore hit genuine gaps in intent) and implement sessions (which hit forks the plan does not settle) can get a ruling on the record rather than inventing one, and so that the question and its answer survive in the run log as evidence.
10	
11	## Being asked a question
12	The model hits a decision it cannot make and puts the question to the user mid-session.
13	- B1: A session's model can request answers from the user by calling a question tool. The tool exists under the same name and with the same request shape on every engine, so a model's behaviour does not change with the engine.
14	  - E9: A question request arrives in a session mode whose tool set excludes the tool → the call is refused with a message the model can act on, not silently ignored.
15	- B2: One request carries one or more questions. Each question has a short header for the card, the question text, and a set of offered options; each option has a label and may carry a one-line explanation.
16	  - E3: Model sends a question with no options → the card shows a free-text-only question; Submit requires non-empty text.
17	- B3: A question is either single-select (exactly one answer) or multi-select (one or more answers), declared per question by the model.
18	- B4: Every question also accepts a free-text answer ("Other") regardless of the offered options, so the user is never forced into a choice the model imagined.
19	  - E1: Multi-select question, user selects several options and also types free text → all selected options and the free text are returned together as that question's answer.
20	  - E2: Single-select question, user types free text instead of choosing → the free text is the answer and no option is reported as chosen.
21	- B5: The transcript shows one card per request, with one group per question in the order the model asked them, and a single Submit for the whole card.
22	  - E7: A second request arrives while one is pending (possible only if the engine allows it) → both cards are shown in arrival order and each is answered on its own; the older one is not silently dropped.
23	- B6: While a request is unanswered the session's status is "needs human" and the session is shown that way in the sessions list and on its tab.
24	  - E5: User switches tabs or closes and reopens the chat view while a card is pending → the card is still there, still pending, and the session is still "needs human".
25	- B14: A session with an unanswered request makes no further progress: it produces no further tool calls or output until the request is resolved.
26	
27	## Answering the card
28	The user reads the card, picks or writes an answer and submits it.
29	- B16: Submit is only possible when every question in the request has at least one answer, either a selected option or non-empty free text.
30	- B13: The answers the model receives are exactly what the user submitted: no option is pre-selected on the user's behalf, no default is applied, no timeout answers for them.
31	- B7: Submitting the card resolves the request: the answers are delivered back to the model as the result of its own tool call, and the session resumes without the user having to send a new prompt.
32	  - E10: The model asks several questions in one request and the user answers them all → the model receives all answers at once as one result, not as several turns.
33	  - E6: The session's engine is no longer alive when the user submits → the answer cannot be delivered; the card is marked as expired-unanswered and the user is told the answer did not reach the session.
34	- B8: A submitted card becomes read-only and keeps showing what was asked and what was answered; a request is resolved at most once, and after resolution — by answer or by cancellation — the card accepts no further input.
35	
36	## Leaving a question unanswered
37	The user does not want to answer, or stops the session while a card is pending.
38	- B12: The user may decline to answer by cancelling or interrupting; the model is told the question was not answered rather than being given a fabricated choice.
39	  - E4: User interrupts the session while a card is pending → the request is cancelled, the card is marked unanswered and read-only, and the session stops as an interrupt would normally stop it.
40	- B15: The model sees the outcome of a request in exactly one of two forms: answered (with the answers) or unanswered (cancelled); it is never left waiting with no result.
41	
42	## Which sessions may ask
43	- B10: With this tool available, plan sessions no longer follow the rule "ask in prose and stop"; a plan session that needs a ruling asks through the tool.
44	- B11: A session that has no user to reach (a sub-session the agent runs on its own behalf) does not get the tool at all.
45	
46	## Reviewing the session afterwards
47	The question and its answer are part of the record, not only of the live view.
48	- B9: The request and its answers are written to the run log the same way any other tool call and result are, in the order they happened, so a transcript replayed from the log shows the question card with its answers.
49	  - E8: The same question request is shown again from a replayed run log → it renders with its recorded answers, read-only, and cannot be re-submitted.
50	
51	## Open questions
52	- Q1: May a question offer a free-text answer *and* selected options in a single-select question, or is free text mutually exclusive with any selection there? (E2 assumes exclusive.)
53	- Q2: Are there caps on the number of questions per request and options per question, and what happens when a model exceeds them — refuse the call or truncate?
54	- Q3: Does the model receive option labels only, or labels plus the fact that the answer came from "Other"? The model may need to distinguish an offered choice from an invented one.
55	- Q4: Should a pending question survive a window reload (sessions are said to survive; engines resume at the next prompt), or is E6 the accepted outcome in that case?
56	- Q5: Is there any notification outside the chat view (status bar, toast) when a background session needs an answer, or is the sessions list enough?
57	- Q6: May the user answer a question with "you decide" explicitly, and if so is that a distinct outcome from cancelling?
58	- Q7: Is the tool available in chat-mode sessions as well as plan and implement sessions?
59	
60	## Findings
61	| Finding | Proposed solution |
62	|---|---|
63	| F1 (contradiction, E6): for the same situation — the engine that asked is gone when the user answers — `SessionManager.respondToPermission` (src/agent/session/session-manager.ts) does not expire the request: it logs the resolution, turns the answer into the next user prompt (`decisionPrompt`) and resumes the session, even re-honouring an allow through `preapproved`. E6 says the answer cannot be delivered, the card is expired-unanswered and the user is told so. If E6 stands, the same session that resumes a permission would refuse to resume a question; the task would be to mark the card expired on delivery failure instead. | Change E6: an answer given after the asking turn is gone is delivered to the session as its next prompt (as a resolved permission already is) rather than thrown away, and only a session that cannot be resumed at all marks the card expired. Losing a decision the user already made is worse than the answer arriving one turn late. |
64	| F2 (breakage, B10): the Goal counts implement sessions among the askers, but only the plan-phase instructions are updated (T11). `implementPrompt` (src/agent/phases/implement.ts) tells the implementer to mark a task ` [blocked: reason]` and move on, and to "stop and say what is needed" — so an implement session would keep blocking rather than ask. The task would be to rewrite those two rules the way T11 rewrites the plan prompt. | Agreed, the spec is too narrow: widen B10 to every session that has a user, and add that an implement session facing a decision only the user can make asks through the tool instead of blocking the task; ` [blocked: reason]` stays for blockers that are not questions (a failing build, a missing dependency). |
65	| F3 (breakage, B10): "ask in prose and stop" is not one rule in `blindPlanPrompt` (src/agent/phases/blind-plan.ts): the direction checkpoint ("A short message, then stop and wait. Write nothing until the user says go") is a deliberate steering gate, and the spec's own `## Open questions` section is where what only the user can answer is recorded. Dropping the prose rule wholesale removes the gate and leaves it unsaid whether an answered question still belongs in Open questions. The spec should say which of the three it replaces. | Narrow B10: it replaces only "when intent does not settle something, ask in prose and stop"; the direction checkpoint stays, because that is the user steering the plan, not the plan asking a question, and `## Open questions` keeps only what is still unanswered — a question the user answered becomes a behaviour or edge case. |
66	| F4 (naive, B11): the code has one sub-session, the mapping run (`ChatViewProvider.startMapping`, mode `reconcile`), and it is started by the user, not by the agent on its own behalf — but it has no transcript: `ChatViewProvider.onSessionEvent` diverts every event of a session with a `parentId` into the plan bar's one-line `followMapping`, while `statusOf` shows the child's status on the parent's tab. So a card from it could never be shown though the tab would read "needs human". The spec should name the mapping run and say it asks through its findings, not through the tool. | Reword B11 to the rule behind it — a session whose output the user never sees as a transcript of its own does not get the tool — and name the mapping run and retrieval sub-sessions as the cases: they report what they could not settle in their result, and the parent session asks. |
67	| F5 (naive, B6): "needs human" does not distinguish a pending question. `nextStatus` (src/agent/session/session-status.ts) already returns `needs_human` on every `turn_done` of a plan, map or implement session, and once set only `user_message` or `permission_resolved` leaves it. So A1's "the status becomes needs human" is usually a no-op, and the sessions list cannot tell a waiting question from a finished turn; resolution also has to restore the working status explicitly. The spec should say how a waiting question is told apart (see Q5). | Change B6 and A1: a pending question is its own session state, distinct in the sessions list and on the tab from a turn that simply ended, and resolving it puts the session back to working; that settles Q5 for the in-product signal and leaves only the out-of-window notification open. A status that means both "done" and "blocked on me" cannot be acted on. |
68	| F6 (naive, B1/B7): the extension's own tools reach Claude through an in-process MCP server (`toolServer`/`toMcpTool`, src/agent/sdk-session/tool-server.ts), and an MCP tool request carries the client's request timeout; the only open-ended human wait this code proves out is `canUseTool`/`SdkSession.requestPermission`, which never times out. A question left on screen for minutes may be abandoned by the engine while the card is still pending. The spec should say what the model is told and what becomes of the card when the engine stops waiting, or require the wait to be kept alive. | Add an invariant: a pending question has no deadline — the wait is held open for as long as the card is unanswered — and if the engine abandons the wait anyway the card stays answerable and falls back to the F1 path. B13 forbids a default, so an expiry would have to mean "unanswered", which throws away a question the user is still looking at. |
69	| F7 (naive, E4/B15): interrupt does not reach a blocked tool on the Claude engine. `SdkSession.interrupt()` only calls `query.interrupt()`; the tool context is built in `buildOptions` with `this.abort.signal`, which fires on `dispose()` alone, and the abort listener that releases a pending request lives in `requestPermission`, on a path the tool does not use. After an interrupt the turn is torn down, so the "not answered" result cannot reach the model as that call's result. The spec should say the model learns of the cancellation on its next turn, not as the tool's own result. | Change E4 and B15: the guarantee is that the model never proceeds on an answer the user did not give, not that a cancelled request answers into the interrupted turn; say the model is told the question went unanswered when it next runs. After an interrupt there is no turn left to answer into. |
70	| F8 (naive, E9): a mode's tool set is not a refusal list. `extension.ts` filters the own tools by name (`allowed(OWN_TOOLS)`) and passes `setup.toolNames` to the engine, so an excluded tool is never offered to the model and there is nothing to refuse on the Claude engine; only `OpenAiSession.runTool` has a fallback ("Unknown tool"). The spec should say that excluding the tool means not offering it. | Agreed: rewrite E9 as "a mode that excludes the tool does not offer it, so no request can arrive", keeping an actionable refusal only for a model that names a tool it was never given. A refusal path for a tool the model cannot see is untestable. |
71

1	import type { ModelProfile } from './model-profile'
2	import type { FileEditChange } from '../edits/file-edit-diff'
3	
4	export type { FileEditChange }
5	
6	/** Token accounting for one assistant turn, as far as the engine reports it. */
7	export type TurnUsage = {
8	  inputTokens: number
9	  outputTokens: number
10	  cacheReadTokens: number
11	  cacheWriteTokens: number
12	  costUsd?: number
13	}
14	
15	/** What an engine is told about one call. Remembering a decision is the host's business, not the engine's. */
16	export type PermissionDecision = { kind: 'allow' } | { kind: 'deny'; message?: string }
17	
18	/**
19	 * What a session emits. One shape for every engine so the UI, the run log and
20	 * later the phase orchestration never see wire formats.
21	 *
22	 * `parentToolUseId` is set on events produced inside a subagent.
23	 */
24	export type SessionEvent =
25	  | { type: 'session_started'; engineSessionId: string; model: string; engineVersion?: string }
26	  | { type: 'user_message'; text: string }
27	  | { type: 'assistant_text'; messageId: string; delta: string; parentToolUseId?: string }
28	  | { type: 'assistant_thinking'; messageId: string; delta: string; parentToolUseId?: string }
29	  /** Final text of an assistant message, replaces whatever was streamed under the same id. */
30	  | { type: 'assistant_message'; messageId: string; text: string; parentToolUseId?: string }
31	  | { type: 'tool_call'; toolUseId: string; name: string; input: unknown; parentToolUseId?: string }
32	  /** `edit` is set on a file edit that changed something: the diff the step made, as the chat shows it. */
33	  | { type: 'tool_result'; toolUseId: string; text: string; isError: boolean; parentToolUseId?: string; edit?: FileEditChange }
34	  | {
35	      type: 'permission_request'
36	      requestId: string
37	      toolName: string
38	      input: unknown
39	      title?: string
40	      description?: string
41	      /** The change the call proposes, shown in place of the raw arguments. */
42	      edit?: FileEditChange
43	    }
44	  | { type: 'permission_resolved'; requestId: string; decision: PermissionDecision['kind'] }
45	  | { type: 'status'; status: 'requesting' | 'compacting' | 'idle' }
46	  | { type: 'turn_done'; usage?: TurnUsage; durationMs?: number; isError: boolean; errors: string[] }
47	  | { type: 'error'; message: string; fatal: boolean }
48	  | { type: 'ended' }
49	
50	export type SessionEventType = SessionEvent['type']
51	
52	/**
53	 * A coding session on one engine. Session-centric on purpose: the extension
54	 * sends prompts and reacts to events; how the engine talks to its model is
55	 * the engine's business.
56	 */
57	export interface CodeSession {
58	  readonly id: string
59	  readonly profile: ModelProfile
60	  /** Queue a user turn. Returns immediately. */
61	  send(text: string): void
62	  /** Single consumer. Ends after the `ended` event. */
63	  events(): AsyncIterable<SessionEvent>
64	  respondToPermission(requestId: string, decision: PermissionDecision): void
65	  /** Stop the current turn; the session stays usable. */
66	  interrupt(): Promise<void>
67	  /** Terminate the engine and release resources. */
68	  dispose(): Promise<void>
69	}
70

1	import type { SessionEvent } from './code-session'
2	import { isPlanning, type SessionMode } from './session-manager'
3	
4	/** What a session is doing right now, as far as the UI needs to know. */
5	export type SessionStatus = 'idle' | 'planning' | 'implementing' | 'needs_human' | 'error'
6	
7	const working = (mode: SessionMode): SessionStatus => (isPlanning(mode) ? 'planning' : 'implementing')
8	
9	/** Derives the next status from an event. Pure, so both the extension host and tests share it. */
10	export function nextStatus(current: SessionStatus, mode: SessionMode, event: SessionEvent): SessionStatus {
11	  switch (event.type) {
12	    case 'user_message':
13	      return working(mode)
14	    case 'status':
15	      if (event.status === 'idle') return current
16	      return current === 'needs_human' ? current : working(mode)
17	    case 'permission_request':
18	      return 'needs_human'
19	    case 'permission_resolved':
20	      return working(mode)
21	    case 'turn_done':
22	      // A phase session that stops has a spec to approve, findings to rule on, questions, or work done or blocked.
23	      if (event.isError) return 'error'
24	      return mode === 'chat' ? 'idle' : 'needs_human'
25	    case 'error':
26	      return event.fatal ? 'error' : current
27	    case 'ended':
28	      return current === 'error' || current === 'needs_human' ? current : 'idle'
29	    default:
30	      return current
31	  }
32	}
33

1	import { z } from 'zod'
2	import type { ToolDefinition } from '../chat-messages'
3	import type { ReadTracker } from './read-tracker'
4	
5	export type ToolContext = {
6	  cwd: string
7	  signal: AbortSignal
8	  files: ReadTracker
9	}
10	
11	export type ToolOutput = { text: string; isError: boolean }
12	
13	export interface Tool<S extends z.ZodObject = z.ZodObject> {
14	  readonly name: string
15	  readonly description: string
16	  readonly schema: S
17	  /** Read-only tools run without asking. */
18	  readonly readOnly: boolean
19	  execute(input: z.infer<S>, ctx: ToolContext): Promise<ToolOutput>
20	}
21	
22	export function toDefinition(tool: Tool): ToolDefinition {
23	  const { $schema: _, ...parameters } = z.toJSONSchema(tool.schema)
24	  return { name: tool.name, description: tool.description, parameters }
25	}
26	
27	export const ok = (text: string): ToolOutput => ({ text, isError: false })
28	export const fail = (text: string): ToolOutput => ({ text, isError: true })
29	
30	/** Tool output past this size is cut; the model can narrow its request. */
31	export const MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS = 30_000
32	
33	export function truncate(text: string): string {
34	  if (text.length <= MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS) return text
35	  return `${text.slice(0, MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS)}\n\n[output truncated at ${MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS} characters]`
36	}

1	import { createSdkMcpServer, tool, type McpSdkServerConfigWithInstance, type SdkMcpToolDefinition } from '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk'
2	import type { z } from 'zod'
3	import type { Tool, ToolContext } from '../openai-session/tools/tool'
4	
5	/**
6	 * The SDK has no tool surface besides MCP, so the tools this extension owns
7	 * reach Claude through an in-process MCP server. No transport or subprocess:
8	 * the handler runs here. The engine names them `mcp__<server>__<tool>`;
9	 * `bareToolName` takes that prefix off again so both engines, the permission
10	 * rules and the transcript speak of the same `JsonQuery`.
11	 */
12	export const TOOL_SERVER_NAME = 'kiwi'
13	
14	const PREFIX = `mcp__${TOOL_SERVER_NAME}__`
15	
16	export function bareToolName(engineName: string): string {
17	  return engineName.startsWith(PREFIX) ? engineName.slice(PREFIX.length) : engineName
18	}
19	
20	export function toolServer(tools: Tool[], ctx: ToolContext): McpSdkServerConfigWithInstance {
21	  return createSdkMcpServer({ name: TOOL_SERVER_NAME, tools: tools.map((t) => toMcpTool(t, ctx)) })
22	}
23	
24	export function toMcpTool<S extends z.ZodObject>(t: Tool<S>, ctx: ToolContext): SdkMcpToolDefinition<S['shape']> {
25	  return tool(
26	    t.name,
27	    t.description,
28	    t.schema.shape,
29	    async (args) => {
30	      const output = await t.execute(args as z.infer<S>, ctx)
31	      return { content: [{ type: 'text', text: output.text }], isError: output.isError }
32	    },
33	    { annotations: { readOnlyHint: t.readOnly } },
34	  )
35	}

1	import type { CodeSession, PermissionDecision, SessionEvent } from './code-session'

5	/**
6	 * `plan` writes a feature's spec blind, `reconcile` checks it against the code
7	 * (together: planning), `implement` builds the approved spec.
8	 */
9	export type SessionMode = 'chat' | 'plan' | 'reconcile' | 'implement'
10	
11	export const isPlanning = (mode: SessionMode): boolean => mode === 'plan' || mode === 'reconcile'
12	
13	export type SessionRecord = {
14	  id: string
15	  title: string
16	  profile: ModelProfile
17	  mode: SessionMode
18	  /** The feature whose spec the session works on; every mode but chat. */
19	  feature?: string
20	  /** The session whose tab this one runs under: a check runs under its plan session and never gets a tab of its own. */
21	  parentId?: string
22	  /** Engine-side conversation id, set once the engine reports it. Lets a closed session continue. */
23	  engineSessionId?: string
24	  createdAt: string
25	}

27	export interface SessionStore {
28	  list(): SessionRecord[]
29	  save(records: SessionRecord[]): Promise<void>
30	}

32	function titleFor(mode: SessionMode, feature: string | undefined): string {
33	  if (!feature) return 'New session'
34	  switch (mode) {
35	    case 'plan':
36	      return `Plan: ${feature}`
37	    case 'reconcile':
38	      return `Map: ${feature}`
39	    case 'implement':
40	      return `Implement: ${feature}`
41	    case 'chat':
42	      return 'New session'
43	  }
44	}

46	export type EngineFactory = (record: SessionRecord) => Promise<CodeSession>
47	
48	export type SessionListener = (sessionId: string, event: SessionEvent) => void
49	
50	/**
51	 * A last pass over an event before it is logged and shown, for what the host
52	 * knows and the engine does not — the diff of a file edit, say. It runs once,
53	 * so what it adds is in the run log and survives a reload.
54	 */
55	export type EventDecorator = (sessionId: string, event: SessionEvent) => Promise<SessionEvent>
56	
57	const noDecoration: EventDecorator = async (_sessionId, event) => event
58	
59	/**
60	 * Owns the list of sessions and the live engines behind them. A session is
61	 * started lazily on its first prompt, and continued from its engine session
62	 * id after the extension host restarted.
63	 */
64	export class SessionManager {
65	  private records: SessionRecord[]
66	  private readonly live = new Map<string, CodeSession>()
67	  /** Per session, the call the user allowed after its engine had stopped; answered for them when the resumed engine asks. */
68	  private readonly preapproved = new Map<string, { toolName: string; input: string }>()
69	
70	  constructor(
71	    private readonly store: SessionStore,
72	    private readonly createEngine: EngineFactory,
73	    private readonly runLogFor: (sessionId: string) => RunLog,
74	    private readonly listener: SessionListener,
75	    private readonly decorate: EventDecorator = noDecoration,
76	  ) {
77	    // Records written before modes existed are chat sessions.
78	    this.records = store.list().map((r) => ({ ...r, mode: r.mode ?? 'chat' }))
79	  }
80	
81	  list(): SessionRecord[] {
82	    return [...this.records]
83	  }
84	
85	  get(id: string): SessionRecord | undefined {
86	    return this.records.find((r) => r.id === id)
87	  }
88	
89	  isLive(id: string): boolean {
90	    return this.live.has(id)
91	  }
92	
93	  /** The live session running under another one's tab, if any. */
94	  liveChildOf(parentId: string): SessionRecord | undefined {
95	    return this.records.find((r) => r.parentId === parentId && this.live.has(r.id))
96	  }
97	
98	  async create(profile: ModelProfile, mode: SessionMode = 'chat', feature?: string, parentId?: string): Promise<SessionRecord> {
99	    const record: SessionRecord = {
100	      id: crypto.randomUUID(),
101	      title: titleFor(mode, feature),
102	      profile,
103	      mode,
104	      ...(feature ? { feature } : {}),
105	      ...(parentId ? { parentId } : {}),
106	      createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
107	    }
108	    this.records.unshift(record)
109	    await this.store.save(this.records)
110	    return record
111	  }
112	
113	  async send(id: string, text: string): Promise<void> {
114	    const record = this.require(id)
115	    if (record.title === 'New session') {
116	      record.title = text.length > 60 ? text.slice(0, 57) + '...' : text
117	      await this.store.save(this.records)
118	    }
119	    ;(await this.ensureLive(record)).send(text)
120	  }
121	
122	  /**
123	   * A request the engine still holds is answered in place. One the engine let
124	   * go of (it stopped with the prompt open, say over a window reload) resumes
125	   * the session: the decision becomes the next user turn, and an allow is
126	   * honoured once more should the resumed engine ask for the same call again.
127	   */
128	  async respondToPermission(id: string, requestId: string, decision: PermissionDecision): Promise<void> {
129	    const live = this.live.get(id)
130	    if (live) {
131	      live.respondToPermission(requestId, decision)
132	      return
133	    }
134	    const record = this.require(id)
135	    const request = await this.openRequest(record, requestId)
136	    if (!request) throw new Error(`Permission request ${requestId} is no longer open`)
137	    await this.emit(record, { type: 'permission_resolved', requestId, decision: decision.kind })
138	    if (decision.kind === 'allow') this.preapproved.set(id, { toolName: request.toolName, input: JSON.stringify(request.input) })
139	    await this.send(id, decisionPrompt(request, decision))
140	  }
141	
142	  async interrupt(id: string): Promise<void> {
143	    await this.live.get(id)?.interrupt()
144	  }
145	
146	  /** Stop the engine but keep the record; a later prompt resumes it. A run under the session stops with it. */
147	  async close(id: string): Promise<void> {
148	    for (const child of this.records.filter((r) => r.parentId === id)) await this.close(child.id)
149	    const session = this.live.get(id)
150	    if (!session) return
151	    this.live.delete(id)
152	    await session.dispose()
153	  }
154	
155	  async remove(id: string): Promise<void> {
156	    await this.close(id)
157	    this.records = this.records.filter((r) => r.id !== id && r.parentId !== id)
158	    await this.store.save(this.records)
159	  }
160	
161	  transcript(id: string): Promise<SessionEvent[]> {
162	    return this.runLogFor(id)
163	      .read()
164	      .then((entries) => entries.map((e) => e.event))
165	  }
166	
167	  async disposeAll(): Promise<void> {
168	    await Promise.all([...this.live.keys()].map((id) => this.close(id)))
169	  }
170	
171	  private require(id: string): SessionRecord {
172	    const record = this.get(id)
173	    if (!record) throw new Error(`Unknown session ${id}`)
174	    return record
175	  }
176	
177	  private async ensureLive(record: SessionRecord): Promise<CodeSession> {
178	    const existing = this.live.get(record.id)
179	    if (existing) return existing
180	    const session = await this.createEngine(record)
181	    this.live.set(record.id, session)
182	    void this.pump(record, session)
183	    return session
184	  }
185	
186	  private async pump(record: SessionRecord, session: CodeSession): Promise<void> {
187	    const log = this.runLogFor(record.id)
188	    for await (const raw of session.events()) {
189	      // A decoration that fails must not cost the event itself.
190	      const event = await this.decorate(record.id, raw).catch(() => raw)
191	      if (event.type === 'session_started' && record.engineSessionId !== event.engineSessionId) {
192	        record.engineSessionId = event.engineSessionId
193	        await this.store.save(this.records)
194	      }
195	      log.append(event).catch((error: unknown) => {
196	        const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)
197	        this.listener(record.id, { type: 'error', message: `Run log write failed: ${message}`, fatal: false })
198	      })
199	      this.listener(record.id, event)
200	      this.answerPreapproved(record.id, session, event)
201	    }
202	    if (this.live.get(record.id) === session) this.live.delete(record.id)
203	  }
204	
205	  /** The allow given after a restart covers one call, in the turn it resumed; anything else is the user's to decide. */
206	  private answerPreapproved(id: string, session: CodeSession, event: SessionEvent): void {
207	    const approved = this.preapproved.get(id)
208	    if (!approved) return
209	    if (event.type === 'turn_done' || event.type === 'ended') {
210	      this.preapproved.delete(id)
211	      return
212	    }
213	    if (event.type !== 'permission_request') return
214	    if (event.toolName !== approved.toolName || JSON.stringify(event.input) !== approved.input) return
215	    this.preapproved.delete(id)
216	    session.respondToPermission(event.requestId, { kind: 'allow' })
217	  }
218	
219	  /** An event of the session's own, outside its engine: logged and shown like the engine's. */
220	  private async emit(record: SessionRecord, event: SessionEvent): Promise<void> {
221	    await this.runLogFor(record.id).append(event)
222	    this.listener(record.id, event)
223	  }
224	
225	  /** The request as logged, if nothing has decided it since. */
226	  private async openRequest(record: SessionRecord, requestId: string): Promise<PermissionRequest | undefined> {
227	    let request: PermissionRequest | undefined
228	    for (const event of await this.transcript(record.id)) {
229	      if (event.type === 'permission_request' && event.requestId === requestId) request = event
230	      if (event.type === 'permission_resolved' && event.requestId === requestId) request = undefined
231	    }
232	    return request
233	  }
234	}
235	
236	type PermissionRequest = Extract<SessionEvent, { type: 'permission_request' }>
237	
238	/** The decision as the model hears it once the engine that asked is gone: the call is named in full so nothing rests on what the resumed engine remembers. */
239	export function decisionPrompt(request: PermissionRequest, decision: PermissionDecision): string {
240	  const call = `the \`${request.toolName}\` call you proposed`
241	  const input = `\`\`\`json\n${JSON.stringify(request.input, null, 2)}\n\`\`\``
242	  switch (decision.kind) {
243	    case 'allow':
244	      return `Go ahead with ${call}; it is allowed.\n\n${input}`
245	    case 'deny':
246	      return `Do not make ${call}; it is denied${decision.message ? `: ${decision.message}` : ''}.\n\n${input}`
247	  }
248	}

22	  connectedCallback(): void {
23	    if (this.childElementCount === 0) {

25	      this.statusLine.className = 'status'
26	      this.appendChild(this.statusLine)
27	    }
28	  }

30	  reset(events: SessionEvent[]): void {
31	    this.replaceChildren(this.statusLine)

37	    this.busy = false
38	    this.setStatus('')

40	    // Streamed text is rendered once at the end of a replay, not per delta.

62	      }
63	      case 'assistant_thinking': {

import { join } from 'node:path'
import type { Scope } from './scope-guard'

export const DOCS_DIR = 'docs'
export const PLAN_DIR = 'plan'

export function featureSlug(feature: string): string {
  return (
    feature
      .toLowerCase()
      .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')
      .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '')
      .slice(0, 60) || 'feature'
  )
}

export function specPath(cwd: string, feature: string): string {
  return join(cwd, PLAN_DIR, `${featureSlug(feature)}.spec.md`)
}

/** The product's front door counts as intent: what it says it is, not how it is built. */
export const README_GLOB = '{README,ReadMe,Readme,readme}.md'

/** `ignored` comes from the `kiwiAgent.planIgnore` setting: docs the planner must not see. */
export function blindPlanScope(feature: string, ignored: string[] = []): Scope {
  const slug = featureSlug(feature)
  // The review file holds the human's comments and the planner's resolutions to them.
  // The intent file holds amendments to `docs/**` the planner proposes; the human applies them.
  const own = [`${PLAN_DIR}/${slug}.spec.md`, `${PLAN_DIR}/${slug}.review.md`, `${PLAN_DIR}/${slug}.intent.md`]
  return {
    readable: [`${DOCS_DIR}/**`, README_GLOB, ...own],
    writable: own,
    ignored,
  }
}

/** Tools a blind planner gets, by name, on either engine. Edit is for answering a comment in place. */
export const BLIND_PLAN_TOOLS = ['Read', 'Glob', 'JsonSchema', 'JsonQuery', 'Write', 'Edit']

/**
 * Phase 1 system prompt. Short on purpose: it states the job and the output
 * contract and leaves the reasoning to the model. Direction is proposed in
 * chat before any file is written, so the user steers while it is cheap.
 */
export function blindPlanPrompt(feature: string, cwd: string): string {
  const slug = featureSlug(feature)
  return `You are planning the feature "${feature}" for a software product, blind to its source code.

Why blind: a planner that reads the code inherits the code's mistakes as constraints, and the feature gets shaped to fit the defects. You derive what the feature should do from intent alone, so that a later phase can compare intent with the code and name every disagreement instead of silently absorbing it.

What you may read: \`${DOCS_DIR}/**\` (product intent: goals, ubiquitous language, rules, constraints, feature descriptions), the README in the workspace root (what the product is, in its own words) and your own output file. Nothing else exists for you; do not try. Use Glob with path \`${DOCS_DIR}\` to see what is there, then Read what is relevant.

Your input: the user's first message describes the feature or user story. Later messages steer, answer your questions or ask for changes.

First, direction. In chat, not in a file: the few decisions that shape the feature (what it is, what it is not, where it could go two ways and which way you propose, with the reason) and the questions whose answer would change that. A short message, then stop and wait. Write nothing until the user says go: a full plan in the wrong direction is wasted, so the user steers first.

Then, the spec. When the user accepts or adjusts the direction, write one file, \`${PLAN_DIR}/${slug}.spec.md\` under ${cwd}, with Write. Structure:

\`\`\`markdown
---
feature: ${feature}
status: draft
---

# ${feature}

## Goal
One paragraph: who, what, why. Domain language only.

## Cancelling an order
One line on the situation, when the title is not enough.
- B1 (${DOCS_DIR}/intent/orders.md#Cancellation): one observable rule, written so a test can prove it
  - E1: situation → expected outcome, an edge of B1
- B2: a rule intent is silent on, settled by you as the sensible default

## Open questions
- Q1: something intent does not settle and only the user can
\`\`\`

The spec is a contract, and the extension holds you to it on every write:
- \`## Goal\` first, as prose. Then one \`##\` section per scenario: a situation from the user's side, named as the user would say it. A small feature has one scenario; a feature is rarely more than four.
- A scenario holds behaviours, \`- B1: ...\`, the rules that make up the situation. An edge case, \`  - E1: ...\`, is indented under the behaviour it qualifies: it is a situation that rule has to survive. An edge case that is a rule of its own is a behaviour. Nothing nests deeper.
- Behaviours are few and coarse, each one something a single test can prove. There are no invariants, acceptance criteria or task sections: an invariant is a behaviour, an acceptance criterion restates one, and the tests that prove each item are the implementer's evidence, recorded on the tasks later. Anything else is reported back to you as off contract.
- Only Goal and one scenario are always there. Open questions exists when there is one.

Rules:
- To the point, not complete. An item earns its place only if leaving it out would change what gets built or how it is tested. Do not restate a behaviour as an edge case, do not spec the obvious, do not cover every situation that could be imagined. A feature described in two sentences is usually a page, not five.
- No tasks: what to do and where is settled when the spec is mapped against the code, in a file of its own. A task written blind would only restate the behaviours.
- Settle what you can. Where intent is silent but a sensible default exists, take it and say so in the direction; a question is for what only the user can answer.
- Item ids (B1, E1, Q1) are global and stable: never renumber on revision, never reuse, only add or mark an item removed. Moving an item to another scenario keeps its id.
- An item that comes from a section of \`${DOCS_DIR}/**\` cites it in parentheses after the id, as \`path#Heading\`. An item without a citation is your own default. The citation is what a later check against the code reads instead of the docs, so it must be exact.
- No code paths, class names or code: that is the implementation's business and you cannot know it. No tables; the Findings table below is not yours.
- A \`## Findings\` section may appear in the file, written by a separate check of the spec against the code: a table with the columns Finding and Proposed solution, one row per finding (F1, F2, ...). Each is something the user rules on. When asked, fill in the Proposed solution cell of each open finding with Edit: how the spec should change, or why it should stand as written, with the reason, in one or two sentences. A proposal is not a ruling: change no item until the user has ruled; then revise the items the finding names per the ruling and append \` [resolved]\` to its Finding cell. Leave the Finding column otherwise alone.
- When a ruling settles something that \`${DOCS_DIR}/**\` does not say, or says otherwise, record the amendment in \`${PLAN_DIR}/${slug}.intent.md\` in the form below. You never edit \`${DOCS_DIR}/\` yourself: intent is the user's, and the user applies these. Record only what outlives this feature — a rule, a term, a constraint — never the feature's own plan.

\`\`\`markdown
## A1 (append) ${DOCS_DIR}/intent/orders.md#Cancellation
- from: F3, ruled for the spec
- why: intent does not say what happens to a cancelled order's reservation.

Cancelling an order releases its reservation immediately.
\`\`\`

  The mode is \`append\` (add to the section), \`replace\` (rewrite the section's body) or \`new\` (add a section, or a document that is not there yet). Write the amendment as intent reads: the product's language, present tense, no reference to this spec or its ids. Amendment ids are stable and never reused; leave an applied one alone.
- The user reviews the draft by commenting on its items and striking the ones that should not be built; comments, strikes and your answers to them live in \`${PLAN_DIR}/${slug}.review.md\`. A submitted review is direction, not a question: revise the spec as it asks, mark every struck item removed without renumbering anything, never bring a struck item back on your own, and answer every comment in that file as addressed or disagreed with a reason.
- If ${DOCS_DIR} has nothing on this feature, or the description is too thin to derive a direction, do not invent: ask, and stop.
- After each write, summarise what changed in a few sentences and stop.`
}

/**
 * The first message of a plan session picked up on a spec another session
 * wrote: the files are the state, so the planner reads them and reports where
 * the plan stands instead of starting the feature over.
 */
export function resumePlanPrompt(feature: string): string {
  const slug = featureSlug(feature)
  return [
    `The spec for "${feature}" already exists at \`${PLAN_DIR}/${slug}.spec.md\`, written in an earlier session that is gone. Do not start over.`,
    '',
    `Read it from disk, and \`${PLAN_DIR}/${slug}.review.md\` and \`${PLAN_DIR}/${slug}.intent.md\` where they exist. Then, in chat, where the plan stands in a few sentences: its status, open questions, findings without a ruling, comments not yet answered. An approved spec is settled: change nothing in it unless the user asks.`,
    '',
    'Then stop; the user says what happens next.',
  ].join('\n')
}

/**
 * The message the planner gets when a spec is off contract: rearrange, do not
 * re-plan. Written for a spec from before the contract as much as for a slip,
 * so it says where invariants, acceptance criteria and flat edge cases go.
 */
export function migrateSpecPrompt(feature: string, problems: string[]): string {
  const spec = `${PLAN_DIR}/${featureSlug(feature)}.spec.md`
  return [
    `The spec for "${feature}" at \`${spec}\` is off contract:`,
    ...problems.map((p) => `- ${p}`),
    '',
    'Read it from disk and rewrite it to the contract with Write, changing the arrangement and nothing else: the rules stay the rules.',
    '- Group the behaviours into scenarios, one `##` per situation from the user\'s side; a small feature has one.',
    '- Nest every edge case under the behaviour it qualifies, indented as `  - E1: ...`. An edge case that qualifies no single behaviour is a behaviour of its own.',

    '- A `## Tasks` section is deleted: tasks live in the tasks file.',
    '- Every B, E, Q and F id that survives keeps its id; Open questions and Findings stay as they are.',
    '',
    'Then, in chat, one line per item that moved or was folded. Then stop.',
  ].join('\n')
}

/** The message the planner gets when a check has written findings: propose, do not rule. */
export function findingsHandoffPrompt(feature: string, findingIds: string[]): string {
  const spec = `${PLAN_DIR}/${featureSlug(feature)}.spec.md`
  return [
    `The check of the spec against the code wrote findings ${findingIds.join(', ')} into the Findings table of \`${spec}\`.`,
    '',
    `Read the spec from disk. For each of these findings, fill in its Proposed solution cell with Edit: how the spec should change, or why it should stand as written, with the reason, in one or two sentences. Change nothing else: the user rules on each proposal, and only then are items revised.`,
    '',
    'Then stop; the user reads the table.',
  ].join('\n')
}

export const IMPLEMENT_TOOLS = ['Read', 'Write', 'Edit', 'Glob', 'Grep', 'JsonSchema', 'JsonQuery', 'Bash', 'Skill']

/** The first prompt of an implement session; the system prompt carries the instructions. */
export const IMPLEMENT_KICKOFF = 'Implement the spec, task by task.'

/**
 * Approval is the human's act; an implementer never starts on anything less,
 * and never starts again on a board whose every task is tested — a fresh
 * session would re-read the code and decide for itself what to redo.
 */
export function assertImplementable(spec: SpecState, tasks: TasksState): void {
  if (!spec.exists) throw new Error('No spec to implement: plan the feature first.')
  if (spec.status !== 'approved') throw new Error('The spec is not approved: rule on the findings and approve it first.')
  if (!tasks.exists) throw new Error('No tasks to implement: map the spec against the code first.')
  if (tasksDone(tasks.tasks)) {
    throw new Error('Every task is tested: plan the next change as its own feature rather than reopening this one.')
  }
}

/**
 * Implement system prompt. The spec is the contract and the tasks file the
 * board: progress is written back into it, so it survives a fresh session.
 */
export function implementPrompt(feature: string, cwd: string): string {
  const spec = `${PLAN_DIR}/${featureSlug(feature)}.spec.md`
  const tasks = tasksFile(feature)
  return `You are implementing the feature "${feature}" from its approved spec at \`${spec}\` under ${cwd}, task by task from \`${tasks}\`.

Where the spec is silent, do the simplest thing that satisfies it and note the choice in one line under the task.

The tasks file is the board. Each task names the spec items it delivers and the files it touches. Work through it in order; a task's state is a marker appended to its line, and you move it along as you go:
- \` [in progress]\` when you start it;
- \` [done]\` when the code is written;
- \` [tested]\` when every item the task delivers is proven by a passing test named on the task's \`proves:\` line;
- \` [blocked: reason]\` when you cannot finish it; then move on.

The \`proves:\` line is the evidence the user reads on the spec: one entry per delivered item, \`<item id> <test file> <test name>\`, comma-separated, the test's name stating the rule it proves:

\`\`\`markdown
- T1 (B1, E1): add the cancel command [tested]
  - files: src/orders/cancel.ts, test/orders/cancel.test.ts
  - proves: B1 test/orders/cancel.test.ts an_open_order_can_be_cancelled, E1 test/orders/cancel.test.ts a_shipped_order_cannot_be_cancelled

Keep the task's \`files:\` line true to what you touched: add a file you needed that the board did not name. When nothing more can be done without the user, stop and say what is needed.

- Shell commands already run in ${cwd}; do not cd there.
- Tested means the tests for the task's items pass, not that you stopped. When every task is tested or blocked, summarise in a few sentences and stop; the whole test suite is run for you once the board is all tested.`

    this.addEventListener(SpecMapRequestedEvent.type, () => post({ type: 'map_spec' }))
    this.addEventListener(SpecMapStoppedEvent.type, () => post({ type: 'stop_map' }))
    this.addEventListener(SpecRepairRequestedEvent.type, () => post({ type: 'repair_spec' }))
    this.addEventListener(ImplementRequestedEvent.type, () => post({ type: 'implement_spec' }))
    this.addEventListener(VerifyRequestedEvent.type, () => post({ type: 'verify_spec' }))
    this.addEventListener(IntentUpdateRequestedEvent.type, () => post({ type: 'update_intent' }))
    this.addEventListener(PlanViewSelectedEvent.type, (e) => this.show(e.view))

    this.addEventListener(PromptSubmittedEvent.type, (e) => post({ type: 'send', text: e.text }))
    this.addEventListener(InterruptRequestedEvent.type, () => post({ type: 'interrupt' }))
    this.addEventListener(PermissionDecidedEvent.type, (e) =>
      post({ type: 'permission', requestId: e.requestId, decision: e.decision }),
    )
    this.addEventListener(AllowWritesToggledEvent.type, (e) => post({ type: 'set_allow_writes', enabled: e.enabled }))
    this.addEventListener(SessionSelectedEvent.type, (e) => {
      this.showCreating(false)
      post({ type: 'switch_session', sessionId: e.sessionId })
    })
    this.addEventListener(SessionClosedEvent.type, (e) => post({ type: 'close_session', sessionId: e.sessionId }))
    this.addEventListener(NewSessionViewRequestedEvent.type, () => this.showCreating(true))
    this.addEventListener(PlanResumeRequestedEvent.type, (e) => post({ type: 'resume_plan', feature: e.feature }))
    this.addEventListener(NewSessionRequestedEvent.type, (e) =>
      post({
        type: 'new_session',
        mode: e.mode,
        ...(e.feature ? { feature: e.feature } : {}),
        ...(e.prompt ? { prompt: e.prompt } : {}),
      }),
    )

    onMessage((message) => this.receive(message))
    post({ type: 'ready' })
  }

  private receive(message: ToWebview): void {
    switch (message.type) {
      case 'state': {
        const active = message.tabs.find((t) => t.active)
        this.activeSessionId = active?.id
        if (!active && !this.creating) this.showCreating(true)
        this.tabs.update(message.tabs, this.creating)
        this.newSession.update(message.plans)
        this.composer.setSwitches({ allowWrites: message.allowWrites })
        this.plan = message.plan
        this.planView.update(this.plan)
        this.layout()
        break
      }
      case 'transcript':
        if (message.sessionId !== this.activeSessionId) return
        this.showCreating(false)
        this.transcript.reset(message.events)
        // A spec that exists is what the session is about; the conversation is one click away.
        this.show(this.plan?.body ? 'plan' : 'chat')
        this.composer.focusInput()
        break
      case 'event':
        if (message.sessionId !== this.activeSessionId) return
        this.transcript.apply(message.event)
        this.follow(message.event)
        break
      case 'show_new_session':
        this.showCreating(true)
        break
    }
  }

  /** The chat shows while the planner works; its finished spec takes over when the turn ends. */
  private follow(event: SessionEvent): void {
    if (!this.plan) return
    switch (event.type) {
      case 'assistant_text':
      case 'assistant_thinking':
      case 'assistant_message':
      case 'tool_call':
      case 'permission_request':
      case 'error':
        this.show('chat')
        break
      case 'status':
        if (event.status !== 'idle') this.show('chat')
        break
      case 'turn_done':
        if (!event.isError) this.show('plan')
        break
    }
  }

  private show(view: PlanViewName): void {
    this.view = view
    this.layout()
  }

  private layout(): void {
    const plan = this.creating ? undefined : this.plan
    const planShown = this.view === 'plan' && plan?.body !== undefined
    this.planView.hidden = !planShown
    this.transcript.hidden = this.creating || planShown
    this.planBar.update(plan, planShown ? 'plan' : 'chat')
  }

  private showCreating(creating: boolean): void {
    this.creating = creating
    this.newSession.hidden = !creating
    this.composer.hidden = creating
    if (creating) this.newSession.reset()
    this.layout()
  }
}

7	type AssistantBubble = { element: HTMLElement; text: HTMLElement; thinking: HTMLElement; streamed: string; finalParts: string[] }
8	
9	/**
10	 * The conversation as an append-only stream. Events patch the DOM directly:
11	 * streamed text lands in the bubble it belongs to, tool results attach to
12	 * their call, permission cards resolve in place. `reset()` replays history.
13	 */
14	export class ChatTranscript extends HTMLElement {
15	  private readonly bubbles = new Map<string, AssistantBubble>()
16	  private readonly tools = new Map<string, HTMLDetailsElement>()
17	  private readonly permissions = new Map<string, PermissionCard>()
18	  private statusLine!: HTMLElement
19	  private busy = false
20	  private working: { element: HTMLElement; stop: () => void } | undefined
21	
22	  connectedCallback(): void {
23	    if (this.childElementCount === 0) {
24	      this.statusLine = document.createElement('p')
25	      this.statusLine.className = 'status'
26	      this.appendChild(this.statusLine)
27	    }
28	  }
29	
30	  reset(events: SessionEvent[]): void {
31	    this.replaceChildren(this.statusLine)
32	    this.bubbles.clear()
33	    this.tools.clear()
34	    this.permissions.clear()
35	    this.working?.stop()
36	    this.working = undefined
37	    this.busy = false
38	    this.setStatus('')
39	    for (const event of events) this.apply(event, false)
40	    // Streamed text is rendered once at the end of a replay, not per delta.
41	    for (const bubble of this.bubbles.values()) {
42	      if (bubble.finalParts.length === 0) renderMarkdown(bubble.streamed, bubble.text, true)
43	    }
44	    this.showWorking()
45	    this.scrollToEnd()
46	  }
47	
48	  apply(event: SessionEvent, live = true): void {
49	    switch (event.type) {
50	      case 'session_started':
51	        this.setStatus(`${event.model} · Claude Code ${event.engineVersion ?? ''}`.trim())
52	        break
53	      case 'user_message':
54	        this.insert(block('user', event.text))
55	        this.busy = true
56	        break
57	      case 'assistant_text': {
58	        const bubble = this.bubble(event.messageId, event.parentToolUseId)
59	        bubble.streamed += event.delta
60	        if (live && bubble.finalParts.length === 0) renderMarkdown(bubble.streamed, bubble.text, false)
61	        break
62	      }
63	      case 'assistant_thinking': {
64	        const bubble = this.bubble(event.messageId, event.parentToolUseId)
65	        bubble.thinking.hidden = false
66	        bubble.thinking.textContent += event.delta
67	        break
68	      }
69	      case 'assistant_message': {
70	        const bubble = this.bubble(event.messageId, event.parentToolUseId)
71	        bubble.finalParts.push(event.text)
72	        renderMarkdown(bubble.finalParts.join(''), bubble.text, true)
73	        break
74	      }
75	      case 'tool_call':
76	        this.insert(this.toolCall(event), event.parentToolUseId)
77	        break
78	      case 'tool_result': {
79	        const details = this.tools.get(event.toolUseId)
80	        const result = document.createElement('pre')
81	        result.className = event.isError ? 'result error' : 'result'
82	        result.textContent = event.text
83	        if (details) {
84	          if (event.edit) showEdit(details, event.edit)
85	          details.appendChild(result)
86	          details.classList.toggle('failed', event.isError)
87	        } else {
88	          this.insert(result, event.parentToolUseId)
89	        }
90	        break
91	      }
92	      case 'permission_request': {
93	        const card = new PermissionCard()
94	        card.className = 'permission'
95	        this.insert(card)
96	        card.show(event)
97	        this.permissions.set(event.requestId, card)
98	        // The card is the indicator now; a ticking clock would say the model is at work.
99	        this.busy = false
100	        break
101	      }
102	      case 'permission_resolved':
103	        this.permissions.get(event.requestId)?.resolve(event.decision)
104	        this.busy = true
105	        break
106	      case 'status':
107	        // 'idle' also arrives mid-turn (after compaction, between requests); only the turn's end clears busy.
108	        if (event.status !== 'idle') this.busy = true
109	        break
110	      case 'turn_done': {
111	        this.busy = false
112	        const line = document.createElement('p')
113	        line.className = event.isError ? 'turn error' : 'turn'
114	        const usage = event.usage
115	        const parts = []
116	        if (usage) parts.push(formatUsage(usage))
117	        if (usage?.costUsd) parts.push(`$${usage.costUsd.toFixed(4)}`)
118	        if (event.durationMs) parts.push(`${(event.durationMs / 1000).toFixed(1)}s`)
119	        if (event.errors.length) parts.push(event.errors.join('; '))
120	        line.textContent = parts.join(' · ')
121	        this.insert(line)
122	        break
123	      }
124	      case 'error':
125	        this.insert(block(event.fatal ? 'error fatal' : 'error', event.message))
126	        if (event.fatal) this.busy = false
127	        break
128	      case 'ended':
129	        this.busy = false
130	        this.insert(block('ended', 'Engine stopped. The next prompt resumes the conversation.'))
131	        break
132	    }
133	    if (live) {
134	      this.showWorking()
135	      this.scrollToEnd()
136	    }
137	  }
138	
139	  /** A pulsing "Working…" row with elapsed time, kept last, while the model is at work. */
140	  private showWorking(): void {
141	    if (!this.busy) {
142	      this.working?.stop()
143	      this.working?.element.remove()
144	      this.working = undefined
145	      return
146	    }
147	    if (!this.working) {
148	      const row = document.createElement('p')
149	      row.className = 'working'
150	      row.textContent = 'Working…'
151	      const startedAt = Date.now()
152	      const timer = window.setInterval(() => {
153	        row.textContent = `Working… ${Math.round((Date.now() - startedAt) / 1000)}s`
154	      }, 1000)
155	      this.working = { element: row, stop: () => window.clearInterval(timer) }
156	    }
157	    this.appendChild(this.working.element)
158	  }
159	
160	  private bubble(messageId: string, parentToolUseId: string | undefined): AssistantBubble {
161	    const existing = this.bubbles.get(messageId)
162	    if (existing) return existing
163	    const element = document.createElement('article')
164	    element.className = 'assistant'
165	    const thinking = document.createElement('pre')
166	    thinking.className = 'thinking'
167	    thinking.hidden = true
168	    const text = document.createElement('div')
169	    text.className = 'text'
170	    element.append(thinking, text)
171	    this.insert(element, parentToolUseId)
172	    const bubble = { element, text, thinking, streamed: '', finalParts: [] }
173	    this.bubbles.set(messageId, bubble)
174	    return bubble
175	  }
176	
177	  private toolCall(event: Extract<SessionEvent, { type: 'tool_call' }>): HTMLDetailsElement {
178	    const details = document.createElement('details')
179	    details.className = 'tool'
180	    const summary = document.createElement('summary')
181	    summary.textContent = `${event.name} ${summarizeInput(event.input)}`
182	    const input = document.createElement('pre')
183	    input.className = 'input'
184	    input.textContent = JSON.stringify(event.input, null, 2)
185	    details.append(summary, input)
186	    this.tools.set(event.toolUseId, details)
187	    return details
188	  }
189	
190	  /** Subagent output nests under the tool call that spawned it. */
191	  private insert(element: HTMLElement, parentToolUseId?: string): void {
192	    const parent = parentToolUseId ? this.tools.get(parentToolUseId) : undefined
193	    ;(parent ?? this).appendChild(element)
194	  }
195	
196	  private setStatus(text: string): void {
197	    this.statusLine.textContent = text
198	    this.statusLine.hidden = text === ''
199	  }
200	
201	  private scrollToEnd(): void {
202	    this.scrollTop = this.scrollHeight
203	  }
204	}
205	
206	/**
207	 * An edit step shows what it did, open, where every other step shows only its
208	 * name: the edit is the session's output, not its plumbing, and the diff is
209	 * capped so it cannot swallow the transcript. The arguments it was called with
210	 * say nothing the diff does not, so they give way to it.
211	 */
212	function showEdit(details: HTMLDetailsElement, change: Parameters<typeof editDiffView>[0]): void {
213	  details.classList.add('edit-step')
214	  details.open = true
215	  const summary = details.querySelector('summary')
216	  if (summary) {
217	    const name = summary.textContent?.split(' ')[0] ?? ''
218	    summary.replaceChildren(document.createTextNode(`${name} `), fileLink(change))
219	    if (change.added !== undefined || change.removed !== undefined) {
220	      const stats = document.createElement('span')
221	      stats.className = 'stats'
222	      stats.textContent = ` +${change.added ?? 0} −${change.removed ?? 0}`
223	      summary.appendChild(stats)
224	    }
225	  }
226	  const input = details.querySelector('pre.input')
227	  if (input instanceof HTMLElement) input.hidden = true
228	  details.appendChild(editDiffView(change))
229	}
230	
231	function block(className: string, text: string): HTMLElement {
232	  const element = document.createElement('article')
233	  element.className = className
234	  element.textContent = text
235	  return element
236	}
237	
238	function summarizeInput(input: unknown): string {
239	  if (typeof input !== 'object' || input === null) return ''
240	  const record = input as Record<string, unknown>
241	  const key = ['command', 'file_path', 'pattern', 'path', 'query', 'description'].find((k) => typeof record[k] === 'string')
242	  if (!key) return ''
243	  const value = record[key] as string
244	  return value.length > 80 ? value.slice(0, 77) + '...' : value
245	}
246	
247	customElements.define('chat-transcript', ChatTranscript)

32	/**
33	 * Root of the chat UI. Talks to the extension host; children talk to it
34	 * through events. Shows the new-session screen, or the active session: its
35	 * transcript, or in a plan session either the transcript or the spec.
36	 */

38	  private readonly tabs = new SessionTabs()
39	  private readonly planBar = new PlanBar()
40	  private readonly planView = new PlanView()
41	  private readonly newSession = new NewSessionView()
42	  private readonly transcript = new ChatTranscript()
43	  private readonly composer = new ChatComposer()

45	  private creating = false
46	  private plan: PlanState | undefined
47	  private view: PlanViewName = 'chat'
48	
49	  connectedCallback(): void {
50	    if (this.childElementCount > 0) return
51	    this.tabs.className = 'tabs'
52	    this.planBar.className = 'plan-bar'
53	    this.planBar.hidden = true
54	    this.planView.className = 'plan-view'
55	    this.planView.hidden = true
56	    this.newSession.className = 'new-session'
57	    this.transcript.className = 'transcript'
58	    this.composer.className = 'composer'

62	    this.addEventListener(ReviewActionEvent.type, (e) => post(e.action))
63	    this.addEventListener(SpecMapRequestedEvent.type, () => post({ type: 'map_spec' }))
64	    this.addEventListener(SpecMapStoppedEvent.type, () => post({ type: 'stop_map' }))
65	    this.addEventListener(SpecRepairRequestedEvent.type, () => post({ type: 'repair_spec' }))
66	    this.addEventListener(ImplementRequestedEvent.type, () => post({ type: 'implement_spec' }))
67	    this.addEventListener(VerifyRequestedEvent.type, () => post({ type: 'verify_spec' }))
68	    this.addEventListener(IntentUpdateRequestedEvent.type, () => post({ type: 'update_intent' }))
69	    this.addEventListener(PlanViewSelectedEvent.type, (e) => this.show(e.view))
70	
71	    this.addEventListener(PromptSubmittedEvent.type, (e) => post({ type: 'send', text: e.text }))
72	    this.addEventListener(InterruptRequestedEvent.type, () => post({ type: 'interrupt' }))
73	    this.addEventListener(PermissionDecidedEvent.type, (e) =>
74	      post({ type: 'permission', requestId: e.requestId, decision: e.decision }),
75	    )
76	    this.addEventListener(AllowWritesToggledEvent.type, (e) => post({ type: 'set_allow_writes', enabled: e.enabled }))
77	    this.addEventListener(SessionSelectedEvent.type, (e) => {
78	      this.showCreating(false)
79	      post({ type: 'switch_session', sessionId: e.sessionId })
80	    })
81	    this.addEventListener(SessionClosedEvent.type, (e) => post({ type: 'close_session', sessionId: e.sessionId }))
82	    this.addEventListener(NewSessionViewRequestedEvent.type, () => this.showCreating(true))
83	    this.addEventListener(PlanResumeRequestedEvent.type, (e) => post({ type: 'resume_plan', feature: e.feature }))
84	    this.addEventListener(NewSessionRequestedEvent.type, (e) =>

86	        type: 'new_session',
87	        mode: e.mode,
88	        ...(e.feature ? { feature: e.feature } : {}),
89	        ...(e.prompt ? { prompt: e.prompt } : {}),
90	      }),

97	  private receive(message: ToWebview): void {
98	    switch (message.type) {
99	      case 'state': {
100	        const active = message.tabs.find((t) => t.active)
101	        this.activeSessionId = active?.id
102	        if (!active && !this.creating) this.showCreating(true)
103	        this.tabs.update(message.tabs, this.creating)
104	        this.newSession.update(message.plans)
105	        this.composer.setSwitches({ allowWrites: message.allowWrites })
106	        this.plan = message.plan
107	        this.planView.update(this.plan)
108	        this.layout()
109	        break
110	      }
111	      case 'transcript':
112	        if (message.sessionId !== this.activeSessionId) return
113	        this.showCreating(false)
114	        this.transcript.reset(message.events)

116	        this.show(this.plan?.body ? 'plan' : 'chat')

119	      case 'event':

121	        this.transcript.apply(message.event)

137	      case 'tool_call':

144	        break
145	      case 'turn_done':

149	  }

154	  }

5	
6	# User question
7	
8	## Goal
9	A session that cannot proceed without a decision from the person running it asks a structured question instead of guessing or stopping with prose. The model issues a question request through a tool; the transcript shows it as a card with the question, its choices and a free-text alternative; the person answers and the answer returns to the model as the tool's own result, so the session continues in the same turn. This exists so that plan sessions (which are blind and therefore hit genuine gaps in intent) and implement sessions (which hit forks the plan does not settle) can get a ruling on the record rather than inventing one, and so that the question and its answer survive in the run log as evidence.
10	
11	## Being asked a question
12	The model hits a decision it cannot make and puts the question to the user mid-session.
13	- B1: A session's model can request answers from the user by calling a question tool. The tool exists under the same name and with the same request shape on every engine, so a model's behaviour does not change with the engine.
14	  - E9: A question request arrives in a session mode whose tool set excludes the tool → the call is refused with a message the model can act on, not silently ignored.
15	- B2: One request carries one or more questions. Each question has a short header for the card, the question text, and a set of offered options; each option has a label and may carry a one-line explanation.
16	  - E3: Model sends a question with no options → the card shows a free-text-only question; Submit requires non-empty text.
17	- B3: A question is either single-select (exactly one answer) or multi-select (one or more answers), declared per question by the model.
18	- B4: Every question also accepts a free-text answer ("Other") regardless of the offered options, so the user is never forced into a choice the model imagined.
19	  - E1: Multi-select question, user selects several options and also types free text → all selected options and the free text are returned together as that question's answer.
20	  - E2: Single-select question, user types free text instead of choosing → the free text is the answer and no option is reported as chosen.
21	- B5: The transcript shows one card per request, with one group per question in the order the model asked them, and a single Submit for the whole card.
22	  - E7: A second request arrives while one is pending (possible only if the engine allows it) → both cards are shown in arrival order and each is answered on its own; the older one is not silently dropped.
23	- B6: While a request is unanswered the session's status is "needs human" and the session is shown that way in the sessions list and on its tab.
24	  - E5: User switches tabs or closes and reopens the chat view while a card is pending → the card is still there, still pending, and the session is still "needs human".
25	- B14: A session with an unanswered request makes no further progress: it produces no further tool calls or output until the request is resolved.
26	
27	## Answering the card
28	The user reads the card, picks or writes an answer and submits it.
29	- B16: Submit is only possible when every question in the request has at least one answer, either a selected option or non-empty free text.
30	- B13: The answers the model receives are exactly what the user submitted: no option is pre-selected on the user's behalf, no default is applied, no timeout answers for them.
31	- B7: Submitting the card resolves the request: the answers are delivered back to the model as the result of its own tool call, and the session resumes without the user having to send a new prompt.
32	  - E10: The model asks several questions in one request and the user answers them all → the model receives all answers at once as one result, not as several turns.
33	  - E6: The session's engine is no longer alive when the user submits → the answer cannot be delivered; the card is marked as expired-unanswered and the user is told the answer did not reach the session.
34	- B8: A submitted card becomes read-only and keeps showing what was asked and what was answered; a request is resolved at most once, and after resolution — by answer or by cancellation — the card accepts no further input.
35	
36	## Leaving a question unanswered
37	The user does not want to answer, or stops the session while a card is pending.
38	- B12: The user may decline to answer by cancelling or interrupting; the model is told the question was not answered rather than being given a fabricated choice.
39	  - E4: User interrupts the session while a card is pending → the request is cancelled, the card is marked unanswered and read-only, and the session stops as an interrupt would normally stop it.
40	- B15: The model sees the outcome of a request in exactly one of two forms: answered (with the answers) or unanswered (cancelled); it is never left waiting with no result.
41	
42	## Which sessions may ask
43	- B10: With this tool available, plan sessions no longer follow the rule "ask in prose and stop"; a plan session that needs a ruling asks through the tool.
44	- B11: A session that has no user to reach (a sub-session the agent runs on its own behalf) does not get the tool at all.
45	
46	## Reviewing the session afterwards
47	The question and its answer are part of the record, not only of the live view.
48	- B9: The request and its answers are written to the run log the same way any other tool call and result are, in the order they happened, so a transcript replayed from the log shows the question card with its answers.
49	  - E8: The same question request is shown again from a replayed run log → it renders with its recorded answers, read-only, and cannot be re-submitted.
50	
51	## Open questions
52	- Q1: May a question offer a free-text answer *and* selected options in a single-select question, or is free text mutually exclusive with any selection there? (E2 assumes exclusive.)
53	- Q2: Are there caps on the number of questions per request and options per question, and what happens when a model exceeds them — refuse the call or truncate?
54	- Q3: Does the model receive option labels only, or labels plus the fact that the answer came from "Other"? The model may need to distinguish an offered choice from an invented one.
55	- Q4: Should a pending question survive a window reload (sessions are said to survive; engines resume at the next prompt), or is E6 the accepted outcome in that case?
56	- Q5: Is there any notification outside the chat view (status bar, toast) when a background session needs an answer, or is the sessions list enough?
57	- Q6: May the user answer a question with "you decide" explicitly, and if so is that a distinct outcome from cancelling?
58	- Q7: Is the tool available in chat-mode sessions as well as plan and implement sessions?
59	
60	## Findings
61	| Finding | Proposed solution |
62	|---|---|
63	| F1 (contradiction, E6): for the same situation — the engine that asked is gone when the user answers — `SessionManager.respondToPermission` (src/agent/session/session-manager.ts) does not expire the request: it logs the resolution, turns the answer into the next user prompt (`decisionPrompt`) and resumes the session, even re-honouring an allow through `preapproved`. E6 says the answer cannot be delivered, the card is expired-unanswered and the user is told so. If E6 stands, the same session that resumes a permission would refuse to resume a question; the task would be to mark the card expired on delivery failure instead. | Change E6: an answer given after the asking turn is gone is delivered to the session as its next prompt (as a resolved permission already is) rather than thrown away, and only a session that cannot be resumed at all marks the card expired. Losing a decision the user already made is worse than the answer arriving one turn late. |
64	| F2 (breakage, B10): the Goal counts implement sessions among the askers, but only the plan-phase instructions are updated (T11). `implementPrompt` (src/agent/phases/implement.ts) tells the implementer to mark a task ` [blocked: reason]` and move on, and to "stop and say what is needed" — so an implement session would keep blocking rather than ask. The task would be to rewrite those two rules the way T11 rewrites the plan prompt. | Agreed, the spec is too narrow: widen B10 to every session that has a user, and add that an implement session facing a decision only the user can make asks through the tool instead of blocking the task; ` [blocked: reason]` stays for blockers that are not questions (a failing build, a missing dependency). |
65	| F3 (breakage, B10): "ask in prose and stop" is not one rule in `blindPlanPrompt` (src/agent/phases/blind-plan.ts): the direction checkpoint ("A short message, then stop and wait. Write nothing until the user says go") is a deliberate steering gate, and the spec's own `## Open questions` section is where what only the user can answer is recorded. Dropping the prose rule wholesale removes the gate and leaves it unsaid whether an answered question still belongs in Open questions. The spec should say which of the three it replaces. | Narrow B10: it replaces only "when intent does not settle something, ask in prose and stop"; the direction checkpoint stays, because that is the user steering the plan, not the plan asking a question, and `## Open questions` keeps only what is still unanswered — a question the user answered becomes a behaviour or edge case. |
66	| F4 (naive, B11): the code has one sub-session, the mapping run (`ChatViewProvider.startMapping`, mode `reconcile`), and it is started by the user, not by the agent on its own behalf — but it has no transcript: `ChatViewProvider.onSessionEvent` diverts every event of a session with a `parentId` into the plan bar's one-line `followMapping`, while `statusOf` shows the child's status on the parent's tab. So a card from it could never be shown though the tab would read "needs human". The spec should name the mapping run and say it asks through its findings, not through the tool. | Reword B11 to the rule behind it — a session whose output the user never sees as a transcript of its own does not get the tool — and name the mapping run and retrieval sub-sessions as the cases: they report what they could not settle in their result, and the parent session asks. |
67	| F5 (naive, B6): "needs human" does not distinguish a pending question. `nextStatus` (src/agent/session/session-status.ts) already returns `needs_human` on every `turn_done` of a plan, map or implement session, and once set only `user_message` or `permission_resolved` leaves it. So A1's "the status becomes needs human" is usually a no-op, and the sessions list cannot tell a waiting question from a finished turn; resolution also has to restore the working status explicitly. The spec should say how a waiting question is told apart (see Q5). | Change B6 and A1: a pending question is its own session state, distinct in the sessions list and on the tab from a turn that simply ended, and resolving it puts the session back to working; that settles Q5 for the in-product signal and leaves only the out-of-window notification open. A status that means both "done" and "blocked on me" cannot be acted on. |
68	| F6 (naive, B1/B7): the extension's own tools reach Claude through an in-process MCP server (`toolServer`/`toMcpTool`, src/agent/sdk-session/tool-server.ts), and an MCP tool request carries the client's request timeout; the only open-ended human wait this code proves out is `canUseTool`/`SdkSession.requestPermission`, which never times out. A question left on screen for minutes may be abandoned by the engine while the card is still pending. The spec should say what the model is told and what becomes of the card when the engine stops waiting, or require the wait to be kept alive. | Add an invariant: a pending question has no deadline — the wait is held open for as long as the card is unanswered — and if the engine abandons the wait anyway the card stays answerable and falls back to the F1 path. 69	| F7 (naive, E4/B15): interrupt does not reach a blocked tool on the Claude engine. `SdkSession.interrupt()` only calls `query.interrupt()`; the tool context is built in `buildOptions` with `this.abort.signal`, which fires on `dispose()` alone, and the abort listener that releases a pending request lives in `requestPermission`, on a path the tool does not use. After an interrupt the turn is torn down, so the "not answered" result cannot reach the model as that call's result. The spec should say the model learns of the cancellation on its next turn, not as the tool's own result. | Change E4 and B15: the guarantee is that the model never proceeds on an answer the user did not give, not that a cancelled request answers into the interrupted turn; say the model is told the question went unanswered when it next runs. After an interrupt there is no turn left to answer into. |
70	| F8 (naive, E9): a mode's tool set is not a refusal list. `extension.ts` filters the own tools by name (`allowed(OWN_TOOLS)`) and passes `setup.toolNames` to the engine, so an excluded tool is never offered to the model and there is nothing to refuse on the Claude engine; only `OpenAiSession.runTool` has a fallback ("Unknown tool"). 88	- No tasks: what to do and where is settled when the spec is mapped against the code, in a file of its own. A task written blind would only restate the behaviours.
89	- Settle what you can. Where intent is silent but a sensible default exists, take it and say so in the direction; a question is for what only the user can answer.
90	- Item ids (B1, E1, Q1) are global and stable: never renumber on revision, never reuse, only add or mark an item removed. Moving an item to another scenario keeps its id.

Each is something the user rules on. When asked, fill in the Proposed solution cell of each open finding with Edit: how the spec should change, or why it should stand as written, with the reason, in one or two sentences. A proposal is not a ruling: change no item until the user has ruled; then revise the items the finding names per the ruling and append \` [resolved]\` to its Finding cell. 11	 * Approval is the human's act; an implementer never starts on anything less,
12	 * and never starts again on a board whose every task is tested — a fresh
13	 * session would re-read the code and decide for itself what to redo.
14	 */
15	export function assertImplementable(spec: SpecState, tasks: TasksState): void {
16	  if (!spec.exists) throw new Error('No spec to implement: plan the feature first.')
17	  if (spec.status !== 'approved') throw new Error('The spec is not approved: rule on the findings and approve it first.')
18	  if (!tasks.exists) throw new Error('No tasks to implement: map the spec against the code first.')
19	  if (tasksDone(tasks.tasks)) {
20	    throw new Error('Every task is tested: plan the next change as its own feature rather than reopening this one.')
21	  }
