24	/**
25	 * Implement system prompt. The spec is the contract and the tasks file the
26	 * board: progress is written back into it, so it survives a fresh session.
27	 */
28	export function implementPrompt(feature: string, cwd: string): string {
29	  const spec = `${PLAN_DIR}/${featureSlug(feature)}.spec.md`
30	  const tasks = tasksFile(feature)
31	  return `You are implementing the feature "${feature}" from its approved spec at \`${spec}\` under ${cwd}, task by task from \`${tasks}\`.
32	
33	The spec is the contract: goal, behaviour, edge cases, and findings the user has ruled on. A human approved it; do not reinterpret it. Where the code and the spec disagree, the spec wins. Where the spec is silent, do the simplest thing that satisfies it and note the choice in one line under the task.
34	
35	The tasks file is the board. Each task names the spec items it delivers, the files it touches (\`files:\`) and what was read to arrive at it (\`context:\`): the modules those files lean on, the test that shows the pattern, where the term already lives. The mapping has been done; start a task by reading its files and its context, and search the code only for what they do not answer. Work through the board in order; a task's state is a marker appended to its line, and you move it along as you go:
36	- \` [in progress]\` when you start it;
37	- \` [done]\` when the code is written;
38	- \` [tested]\` when every item the task delivers is proven by a passing test named on the task's \`proves:\` line;
39	- \` [blocked: reason]\` when you cannot finish it; then move on.
40	
41	The \`proves:\` line is the evidence the user reads on the spec: one entry per delivered item, \`<item id> <test file> <test name>\`, comma-separated, the test's name stating the rule it proves:
42	
43	\`\`\`markdown
44	- T1 (B1, E1): add the cancel command [tested]
45	  - files: src/orders/cancel.ts, test/orders/cancel.test.ts
46	  - proves: B1 test/orders/cancel.test.ts an_open_order_can_be_cancelled, E1 test/orders/cancel.test.ts a_shipped_order_cannot_be_cancelled
47	\`\`\`
48	
49	Keep the task's \`files:\` line true to what you touched: add a file you needed that the board did not name. When nothing more can be done without the user, stop and say what is needed.
50	
51	A finding whose ruling says to fix the code is work too; do it with the task it touches.
52	
53	Rules:
54	- In the tasks file, only the markers, the files line, the proves line and a one-line note under a task are yours. The spec is not yours to change at all.
55	- Never edit \`${DOCS_DIR}/\`: intent is the user's.
56	- Read a file before editing it; read it again when a tool result says it changed underneath you. Do not re-explore what the context line already names.
57	- Shell commands already run in ${cwd}; do not cd there.
58	- Tested means the tests for the task's items pass, not that you stopped. When every task is tested or blocked, summarise in a few sentences and stop; the whole test suite is run for you once the board is all tested.`
59	}

event.text:
The failing run was my own doing: T9's new prompt test used `blindPlanPrompt` and `implementPrompt` without importing them, and the file was mid-edit when the verification ran, which took the whole worker pool down with it rather than just that file.

What I fixed and finished:

- **T7 [tested]** — the question card: one card per request, a group per question in the order asked, radio/checkbox controls per the single/multi flag, a free-text "Other" on every question, one Submit gated by `canSubmit` that names the unanswered questions, and a read-only card showing the submitted answers (or "Not answered.") once resolved. The transcript drops the raw tool-call row and result for the question tool, and a pending card switches a plan session to the chat view. Proving it needed a DOM, so jsdom is a new devDependency and the two webview test files name their own environment. Two pre-existing type errors from T3 and T5 surfaced with the first typecheck and were fixed.
- **T8 [tested]** — replay: `reset` rebuilds every card from the log, answered ones read-only and unsubmittable, open ones still pending and answerable, several in arrival order, and the same log replays cleanly into the same element on a tab switch or reopened view.
- **T9 [tested]** — `AskUser` is in `OWN_TOOLS`, in the plan and implement tool sets, out of the mapping run's, and read-only so it never prompts. Per F3 the plan prompt asks through the tool instead of "ask, and stop" while keeping the direction checkpoint, and per F2 the implement prompt asks rather than blocking, with `[blocked: reason]` kept for blockers no answer would remove.

`npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build` now passes: 340 tests in 34 files, clean types, clean bundle. Every task on the board is tested.
